blocks.text: On plan and shipped — a second format and a launch call remain
The brief is essentially delivered; the project has already moved into distribute-and-extend.

items: **Built to spec** — the defining epic (#1) is closed; all nine deliverables exist, seven of eight criteria proven.
**Then hardened and released** — a field-eval + distribution wave the brief never scoped shipped a live **v0.4.0**.
**One plan-level gap** — the second harness format (OpenCode, {chip.warn:#12}) is not yet productionized.
**One decision blocks launch** — the public install 404s only because the repo is {warn:private}; going public fixes it, no code change.

notes: Recap what we committed to, so the scorecards that follow have a yardstick. No timelines were ever in the brief — it is deliverables + mechanically-verifiable acceptance criteria.

blocks.text: The brief committed us to two products over one shared schema

items: **Product A — the plugin**: a harness-pure `core/` + `mcp/` boundary, wrapped as **two formats** (Claude Code + OpenCode) from one implementation.
**Product B — the pocket-librarian**: a single Go binary (embedded PocketBase, eino loop), six desk tools as both CLI and MCP server, record-original-first.
**The contract — schema v1** both read, personalized only through `_knowledge/profile.yaml`.
**The hard rule — identity-neutrality as a required CI check**: no name/org/repo/issue token ships except as a `{{profile.…}}` placeholder.
Scored on **9 deliverables + 8 mechanically-verifiable criteria** — no dates, by design.

blocks.text: Most work since the epic was hardening and distribution the brief never scoped

items: **Field-eval hardening (#13–#18)** — record-original-first no longer caps at 5 KB, patrol resolves stale findings, orphan-noise + rule-severity fixes.
**Multi-desk topology (ADR 0002 → #23)** — XDG canonical store home, fail-closed store location, and a desk open-guard so a store can't be opened under the wrong desk.
**Store self-initialization (ADR 0003 → #31)** — tool commands auto-migrate a fresh store; no manual `migrate up` first-run papercut.
**Distribution substrate (#7, #25, #27)** — a `curl`-able `install.sh` with sha256 verification, SHA-pinned GitHub Actions, a `VERSION`-driven release pipeline, three user guides + recorded demos.
**Released v0.4.0** — four platform binaries + checksums + plugin bundle, and the full integration suite now runs in CI and the release gate.

blocks.title: Proven end-to-end
blocks.text: The darwin/arm64 binary downloads, runs, reports v0.4.0, and its sha256 matches the published checksums.

footer: Incident log 2026-07-17 · authed gh release download confirms the assets are valid — the gap is purely visibility
notes: This is the only thing standing between us and the public install story. It is not a bug — install.sh is correct. Every unauthenticated URL the public flow needs 404s only because the repo is private. Making the repo public resolves all of them with zero code change. If it must stay private, install.sh would need token/gh auth (a design change).

blocks.text: The public install path is blocked only by repo visibility, not by code

items: The public `curl | bash` flow fetches `install.sh`, `/releases/latest`, and `/releases/download/…` — all **404 while the repo is {warn:private}**.
install.sh's URL construction and checksum logic are **proven correct**: its URLs are byte-identical to the API's `browser_download_url`, and the authenticated download verifies.
The **only** missing link is the unauthenticated HTTP fetch — i.e. repo visibility.

blocks.title: Decision needed
blocks.text: Make the repo public to unblock #7 (no code change), or add token/gh auth to install.sh if it stays private.

blocks.text: Ahead of the brief on delivery — the roadmap is now launch, not build

items: **Against the brief: delivered.** Epic closed, nine deliverables built, seven of eight criteria proven — plus a released binary the brief never asked for.
**The one open commitment** is the second harness format (OpenCode, #12) — architectural, and it wants an OpenCode-target ruling before fan-out.
**Phase shift.** The project is past 'build to spec' and into distribute-and-extend: launch (go public), the second format (#12), and the SOP template library (#36).
**Health is good** — all design rulings are in (three ADRs), main is CI-green, and everything still open is pure build work, not unresolved questions.

notes: Close on the three calls only Henry can make. The first is the highest-leverage and needs no engineering.

items: **Go public?** — unblocks the public `curl | bash` install, closing #7's last criterion. No code change.
**OpenCode-target ruling** — the shape of the second format, so #12 can fan out and the last plan item lands.
**#36 SOP library direction** — vendor-vs-sync and type↔classification, scoped as the next major bump.

blocks.title: The through-line
blocks.text: The build is done and shipped; what is left is deciding how far to open it and how far to extend it.
